carried_unknowns.description: grant.project_id is compared against packet.repo_binding.project_id (falling back to packet.project when repo_binding is absent) — the C0-R2 program's project-naming convention (e.g. 'dopetask') — not dopeTask's own internal repo-identity project_id ('dopetask.core' from .dopetask/project.json, which guard.identity.assert_repo_binding already checks separately and unconditionally for every packet, governed or not). The grant schema's field description does not pin this down further.

grant.repository is checked as a substring of the active repo's git origin URL (dopetask.guard.identity.extract_origin_url), reusing the same hint-substring convention as guard.identity.origin_hint_warning / repo_binding.origin_hint, but enforced fail-closed here rather than as a soft warning. The schema only types this field as a non-empty string with no pattern or enum, so an exact-match convention was also plausible; substring-of-origin-URL was chosen as the more defensible mapping given the codebase's existing origin_hint precedent.

grant.network_policy and grant.credential_class are Draft-07 schema-validated (their 'insufficient when a grant requires an explicit class' field descriptions are informative, not machine-checkable consts) but are not cross-checked against any additional business rule beyond schema conformance, since S01's explicit requirement list does not name them. provider_ceiling is likewise schema-validated only, never enforced against CLI/packet input (only model_ceiling is, per S02's explicit requirement).

grant.worktree_binding.head_sha (nullable, optional) is not checked against the current repo HEAD. Only worktree_binding.path is verified. Checking head_sha would make every grant go stale the instant a new commit lands on the bound worktree, which is not what S01's 'worktree binding against current repo/worktree identity' requirement appears to intend.
